messages:
maya: Quick follow-up on the slot-aware scheduler RFC — thanks for the feedback yesterday. I sketched an approach to separate admission queues by "slot class" (fast vs batch) and add a small per-slot backlog that can be rebalanced. Main goals: preserve tail-SLO for fast slots, avoid starvation, and make eviction predictable.

ashwin: curious about complexity — can we avoid per-tenant per-slot queues? that's N*M state.

maya: yeah that's the point — we keep tenant-level logical queues but use slot-classes as an admission tag. admission rules map requests->lane without duplicating per-tenant structures. sketch: 

```yaml
admission: 
  map: 
    - match: {latency_hint: <=50ms} -> lane: fast
    - match: {batchable: true} -> lane: batch
  lane_config: 
    fast: {max_inflight: 200, headroom_pct: 15} 
    batch: {max_inflight: 800, batch_timeout_ms: 12}
```

liam: what about KV cache affinity? if we shuffle too aggressively we'll lose cache hits and increase token cost.

maya: good call. added a "hot-key pin" rule — short-circuit to same worker for up to 500ms if KV cache hit recently. It only pins if lane==fast and request_size<2k tokens.

ophira: preemption model? do we interrupt in-flight microbatches or only prevent new ones?

maya: prefer soft-preempt: drain microbatch but mark lane as throttled. If latency SLO violated we can force-evict tail microbatches (configurable). eviction policy: LRU by request-age within lane, but prefer evicting batchable payloads first.

deploy-bot: RFC updated: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/slot-aware-scheduler (edited)

ashwin: can we get simple perf numbers? latency p99 for fast slots with vs without separation.

maya: ran a small sim this morning: separated lanes reduced fast-slot p99 from 180ms -> 95ms at 80% cluster load. batch throughput dropped ~7% but overall token cost ~flat because fast lanes avoided re-computation on evicted KV contexts. I'll attach the sim outputs to the RFC.

liam: nice. action items?

maya: - add unit tests for admission mapping and lane tagging
- sim with KV-hot workloads (vary working set sizes)
- prototype in canary cluster with soft-preempt enabled
- add telemetry: per-lane headroom, drop rates, per-tenant evictions

ophira: +1. I can take Telemetry (define metrics and dashboards).

ashwin: I'll pair on proto (slot mapping + admission codepath).

maya: thanks all. tagging @eng-runtime for awareness.

maya: fyi: one open question — how to surface lane-level backpressure to upstream routers without leaking queue lengths per-tenant. idea: report aggregated headroom per-lane per-az, not per-tenant. open to other suggestions.
